sense: surprise, or not having caught it

terms.comment: Alone, it asks for more or protests; followed by the word that surprised (Quid? jam uxōrem?).
The startled “huh?” of comedy (Lewis & Short: surprise).

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.13.3: quid ais? Caesarem nunc dēfendit Cūriō?
terms.comment: Of surprise or disbelief at what was said; also simply “tell me”. For the disbelieving “really?”, ain’? (see really?).

phrases.latin: Quid? jam uxōrem? — Jam. — Jam? — Jam, quantum potest.
phrases.english: What? a wife now? — Now. — Now?! — Now, as fast as can be.

phrases.latin: Bonō animō es: dūcēs uxōrem hanc. — Hem. — Bonō animō es, inquam.
phrases.english: Cheer up: you’ll marry her. — Huh? — Cheer up, I said.

phrases.latin: quid ais? Caesarem nunc dēfendit Cūriō?
phrases.english: What? Curio is now defending Caesar?

phrases.latin: vocō, quaerō ecquid litterārum. negant. quid ais? inquam, nihilne ā Pompōniō?
phrases.english: I call them, ask if there are any letters. They say no. “What?” I say, “nothing from Pomponius?”
